blocks.text: Fifteen of the sixteen organisations heard raised collaboration, and the channels already exist in JAMS, the bid teams and the tour-operator forums, so the task is to turn existing forums into one joint plan.

Collaboration is one of the two concerns stakeholders share most widely, and the channels for it already work. Fifteen of the 16 organisations heard raised it, as many as raised data sharing (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p20 to p46; a rough count of organisations with at least one collaboration insight, taken from the appendix tables by organisation and not weighted by insight row; section 2.4). FEDHASA reports that Western Cape tourism associations already coordinate through JAMS with Wesgro, the Western Cape Government and the City of Cape Town (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p31). C-BRTA cites biannual tour-operator forums, and the Department of Tourism cites statistics committees that already convene public and private stakeholders (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p28, p37). The province does not need another forum. It needs the forums it has to plan together.

Joint work already pays where the task is concrete. Mossel Bay's cruise calls rose from four before Covid to 27 a season, supported by closer coordination and better excursion packaging (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p20). The town credits its public-private tourism model with faster decisions (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p21). The CTICC finds the same on bids: destination stakeholders collaborate effectively on bid development and international event attraction (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p46).

Growth to 2035 needs that discipline applied to development, and here the system falls short. The West Coast District Municipality finds provincial and regional forums dominated by destination marketing rather than development (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p39). Operators are represented only through LTOs and business chambers, so private participants are sometimes unaware of tourism plans and projects (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p39). The Department of Economic Development reports that misalignment between public tourism institutions and key industry bodies is weakening collaboration (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p25).

blocks.message: Collaboration is wanted almost everywhere and already works in places, but the forums are marketing-led and the trade's voice is missing.

blocks.text: The record describes a system that collaborates to sell and stalls when it must plan. Joint work succeeds on a bid, a cruise call or a route, where the task is bounded and the payoff shared. It weakens on development, where no forum owns the agenda and operators sit one step removed. The airlines and distributors that fill the seats are also absent. No airline, online travel agency or tour operator gave a recorded view (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p16).

Wesgro uses the forums that exist and gives them a development agenda and one joint plan. In 2027 it adopts JAMS as the single channel to the associations, because FEDHASA expects consultation through it to cascade more efficiently than approaching each body separately (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p31). It adds the Tour Guides Association, so frontline operators have a voice (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p31). Sector councils for wine, business events, adventure and culture are designed inside Steerco's structure (section 4.7) and run from 2029 (section 4.3).

Partners carry the regional and bidding work. District municipalities, DEDAT and the LTOs give regional forums a development agenda and tailor provincial support to district needs. The CTICC and the universities supply the academic and sector champions on whom international bids depend (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p46). Nationally, the province asks SA Tourism to include provincial assets in its campaigns for emerging source markets, which Robben Island Museum also seeks (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p33). From 2029 the joint industry plan is agreed and reviewed each year.

blocks.text: A joint plan gives each forum a decision to make, not just information to exchange. Sector councils give wine, business events, adventure and culture a standing seat, so the market, not officials, sets development priorities. Shared targets already pay here. Cape Town secured 36 conference bids in 2024/25, expected to bring more than 27,000 delegates and R745 million in economic impact through 2028 (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p36). Cape Town also added 17 mainline international routes from 2015 to 2025, more than any of eight secondary airports in the comparison. That record is credited to Wesgro's commercial and relationship-driven route development (MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment, Mar 2026, "Executive Summary", "International Comparisons").

Valencia shows the model at destination scale. Sector-led executive committees, with the regional business confederation on the governing board, keep tourism development market-driven rather than bureaucratically led (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p45, p48, p49). Valencia received 3.5 million international visitors in 2024, 24.4% above 2019 (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p46). That performance is credited to governance that is decentralised, sector-led and embedded across the destination (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p60). Singapore's tourism board, airport group and national airline work under one coordinated strategy with shared KPIs (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p40, p42). The condition is commitment from industry. The plan holds only if the associations and the trade sign up, so the number of partners signed up is its measure of success (section 5.2).
